title: Coproduct preservation by exact derived functors
statement:
In Grothendieck abelian categories with unbounded derived categories and the stated K-injective resolution hypotheses, the cochain localization preserves arbitrary small coproducts. An additive exact functor preserving those coproducts induces a functor on unbounded derived categories preserving them as well, in the same indexing universe.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v u' v' w w' s
theorem Functor.mapDerivedCategory_preservesCoproducts
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] [Abelian D] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} D]
    [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions A] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions D]
    [HasCoproducts.{s} A] [HasCoproducts.{s} D]
    (F : A ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (I : Type s) [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F.mapDerivedCategory
```

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21, ordinary evaluation left extension and the subsequence generalization; Stacks 03DA, 03DB, 06YT and 07D9

proof.text: Use the known coproduct cocone of the derived category obtained from termwise coproducts of complexes. Any family of derived objects is represented by a family of complexes. The exact functor factorization identifies its image cocone with localization of the termwise image coproduct; the ordinary preservation hypothesis and localization preservation make this a coproduct. Transport through the representing family isomorphisms.
